title: The teams in the product: the walk on Home, the solution team on a project, every walk on Admin
request: Phase 6 (the owner): Home and the product: the board, the pauses answered on the page, the API for testers.
plan: A service the routes call: start or resume a walk once, read a walk without running it, list the walks.
Routes for drafts, projects and Admin.
A Team panel on Home and a Teams tab on Admin.
The critic's model only after the sealed gate.
The team's switch and budgets as one workspace file, changed by an admin, every change audited (the twin switch's pattern).
Budgets per walk (euros across its resumes, steps) and per node (euros), each walk stopping with the reason the person sees.
Home's Build through the walk when the switch is on: the proposal's solution and settings accepted as before, the build being the walk's approval.
A product flow through the team, and a browser test of the Team panel.

decisions.decision: A step only when the person asks: the page reads the walk, and POST runs it to its next pause.
decisions.why: A walk waits on the person; nothing should run behind their back or twice.

decisions.decision: The pause shown is read from the pauses the walk writes, not from the checkpoint's internals.
decisions.why: The walk already writes each pause open and closes it: one source the page and the dataset both read.

decisions.decision: The critic's model serves only once the team passed its sealed gate.
decisions.why: The measurement decides what serves; until then the rules ask.

decisions.decision: With the switch on, the person's "build it" approves only the walk's build pause; a question, the map's confirmation or the critic's concerns come back to the chat as what the team asks first.
decisions.why: The owner's three interrupts each belong to the person; turning "build it" into an approval of the critic's concerns would override them without the person seeing them.

decisions.decision: The euro budget per walk is checked between nodes from the experience log's requests, and each node's model is capped by the gateway at a node's budget for each start or resume.
decisions.why: A request in flight cannot be stopped; the gateway's own run cap bounds every request, and the walk's check stops it before the next node.

decisions.decision: The switch is off by default.
decisions.why: The team failed its sealed gate (JRN-019): the rules and the direct build serve until the owner turns the team on.

change: dclab_rnd/orchestra/service.py; GET/POST /api/drafts/{id}/team (draft/api.py), GET/POST /api/projects/{id}/team and GET /api/teams (agentic/pages/team.py, the owner's); Home's Team panel and Admin's Teams tab; the API client and the app rebuilt. Then (completing 28.8): dclab_rnd/orchestra/settings.py (team.json: on, run_eur, node_eur, max_steps); GET/PUT /api/team/settings (an admin's, audited) and the Admin Teams tab's switch; the walk stops at its euro budget and after a node over its own, records each node's cost and shows the live spend on its board; the solution team stops at its euro budget; orchestra.service.build_draft and Home's quick build through it when the switch is on; scripts/product_e2e.py flow upload-team; the Team panel follows a build.

findings.defect: The Team panel showed nothing when the walk paused before its first hand-off.
findings.scenario: In the browser: the walk paused on the first question; the page said it had not walked yet.
findings.cause: The panel drew only when a board existed.
findings.fix: The panel shows the waiting pause whether or not a board was written.
findings.test: manual check in the app's browser (screenshots), tests/test_team_api.py

findings.defect: An ML engineer could open the holdout through the new project route.
findings.scenario: A data_scientist posted approve=true while the solution team waited on the holdout gate: the gate was approved and the programme read the holdout.
findings.cause: The route needed only write; the walk approved the gate as the person.
findings.fix: A resume of a holdout approval demands approve_gate (an owner or a reviewer).

findings.defect: The page showed a pause the walk no longer waited on.
findings.scenario: An empty answer ended the walk; the page still showed the question; answering it gave 409.
findings.cause: The pause was read from the last line of the pauses file, which a skipped question never closes.
findings.fix: The pause is read from the walk's checkpoint.

findings.defect: Starting again while a draft's walk waited threw the walk away.
findings.scenario: After two answers, POST {} restarted the walk from nothing; the first left orphaned boards and no record.
findings.cause: The walk did not guard a start against an open pause, as the solution team did.
findings.fix: A start while a pause waits returns that pause; a new walk starts on a fresh thread.

findings.defect: An answer was not checked against its pause.
findings.scenario: approve=false sent to the prediction moment's question recorded the moment as 'False'.
findings.cause: Any body resumed any pause.
findings.fix: A question takes words, a confirmation or an approval a yes or no; anything else 422.

findings.defect: Two runs of a project's team could overlap.
findings.scenario: Two POSTs at the holdout approval both approved the gate; one approval stayed unused for a later read.
findings.cause: The project's running flag is set only inside the programme's run.
findings.fix: One walk of a project at a time (409 otherwise).

findings.defect: Items carried over from 28.3 were dropped silently.
findings.scenario: 28.3's Left moved the team switch and the per-run budget to 28.8; neither was built or listed.
findings.cause: The status was written from what was built.
findings.fix: Listed under 28.8's Left.

findings.defect: An approval was asked without showing what it approves.
findings.scenario: Approve: understanding with Yes and No, the critic's concerns unseen, recorded as overridden.
findings.cause: The view dropped the pause's summary.
findings.fix: The pause's summary (the concerns, the parts, the build's state) shown, escaped.

findings.defect: Two quick resumes could lose a session from the walk's record.
findings.scenario: The state was read before the turn lock; the second request rewrote runs from a stale read; the spend and models under-counted.
findings.cause: The read and the walk were not under one lock; runs was overwritten.
findings.fix: The read is inside the turn; runs is appended by a reducer.

findings.defect: The busy check blocked the event loop on PostgreSQL.
findings.scenario: answering() opened a connection on the loop.
findings.cause: Called directly in the async route.
findings.fix: Run in a thread, as the message route does.

findings.defect: A test would fail the day the sealed team run passes.
findings.scenario: It asserted the critic's model never serves, from the repository's evidence.
findings.cause: A fact of the evidence asserted as a constant.
findings.fix: team_passed patched in the test.

findings.defect: The dev corpus was not rebuilt.
findings.scenario: test_devlog: train.chat.jsonl stale.
findings.cause: make sft-dev not run after the record.
findings.fix: The dev corpus rebuilt with make sft-dev after the record.

findings.defect: Failure paths were untested.
findings.scenario: No test for the project route, a wrong answer, a restart, the holdout permission.
findings.cause: Only the happy path was tested.
findings.fix: Tests for each.

findings.defect: The new write routes did not say what they record.
findings.scenario: check-commit on 14f8383: test_experience_log listed POST /api/drafts/{id}/team and /api/projects/{id}/team as write routes with no declared record.
findings.cause: Every write route must name the events it writes; the routes were added without the entry.
findings.fix: Both declared: the walk's team.handoff and team.interrupt events (team.recorded at its end).

findings.defect: The new write route said nothing of what it records.
findings.scenario: The rule that every write route says what it records failed on the team settings route.
findings.cause: The route was added without its entry.
findings.fix: The route records a policy decision, as the twin switch does.

findings.defect: With the switch on, "build it" in the chat locked the draft for ever.
findings.scenario: The Home agent's turn holds the draft's lock; its build ran the walk in another thread, which waited on that lock; every later chat turn on the draft was stuck until a restart.
findings.cause: The build from the chat handed the walk to a worker thread.
findings.fix: From the chat the walk runs in the thread that holds the turn (the lock is re-entrant within a thread).
findings.test: upload-team (the product flow through the chat's build)

findings.defect: The walk's euro budget never counted the Home agent's model requests.
findings.scenario: Thirty answered questions at five cents each spent EUR 1.50 against a budget of EUR 0.50 and the walk never stopped.
findings.cause: The Home agent's own run rebinds the run id, so its requests carried another run than the walk's.
findings.fix: The walk binds its run as the parent of every request made inside it, and counts a request of its run or of a run inside it.

findings.defect: A node's budget capped a whole start or resume, not one node.
findings.scenario: Two nodes of one resume at EUR 0.15 each: the second was refused although neither passed its budget.
findings.cause: The cap was set once per start or resume.
findings.fix: Before each node the models' caps are set to what they had spent plus one node's budget.

findings.defect: "Build it" could approve the critic's concerns for the person.
findings.scenario: A build approved in one tab situated the walk again onto the critic's gate; a Build pressed in another tab resumed it with a bare yes.
findings.cause: The resume was an answer to whatever pause was open.
findings.fix: The resume is keyed to the build pause that was read; another pause asks again.

findings.defect: Two Build presses at once gave a server error.
findings.scenario: Both reached the build pause; the second found nothing to resume and raised.
findings.cause: A resume with no pause raised past the build.
findings.fix: A pause already answered by another request reads the draft again and returns its project.

findings.defect: Approving the build on the Team panel built a project whose stages never started.
findings.scenario: The panel resumed the walk directly, without the step that starts the agent on the project.
findings.cause: The panel's approval did not go through Build.
findings.fix: The panel's build approval calls Build with the team, which the walk takes as its approval, and the agent starts.
findings.test: team (the browser check of the Team panel)

findings.defect: The team flow read the walk's record too early.
findings.scenario: The draft gets its project inside the build node; the walk writes its end record a moment later, and the flow read none.
findings.cause: The flow checked the record as soon as the project appeared.
findings.fix: The flow waits for the walk's end record and for the chat's build message, then follows the agent's stages.
findings.test: upload-team (the product flow through the chat's build)

findings.defect: The panel's build approval skipped the walk when the switch was off.
findings.scenario: Walking with the team on Home and approving its build built directly, leaving the walk waiting on its approval.
findings.cause: Build followed the switch alone.
findings.fix: Build takes the panel's approval through the walk whatever the switch.
findings.test: team (the browser check of the Team panel)

findings.defect: Build through the team asked for a single outcome on a problem of several parts.
findings.scenario: A fraud problem drawn as several parts with a file of known cases was refused for want of an outcome column.
findings.cause: The step that accepts a single solution ran before the walk.
findings.fix: Through the team, a problem with no single named outcome is left to the walk's own build, which handles several parts.
findings.test: team (the browser check of the Team panel)

findings.defect: With the switch on, a question answered in the chat never cleared the walk's pause, so build it repeated the answered question for ever.
findings.scenario: The person answered the outcome question in the chat and said build it again; each time the chat said the team asks first which column is the outcome, and only the Team panel could unstick the walk.
findings.cause: Home's build through the team refused on any pause that was not the build's approval, even one the person had settled elsewhere; and the map's confirmation did not look at the draft again.
findings.fix: A question whose field and words are no longer the draft's open question, or a map confirmed elsewhere, is resumed with a key no pause has, so the walk reads the draft again and moves on or asks what is open now; the critic's concerns are never looked past, and the chat says what they are and where to decide.

findings.defect: Every error raised inside the walk was reported as a pause another request had answered.
findings.scenario: A build that failed on a changed table after its project was made said another request answered the team's pause, and the real reason was lost.
findings.cause: The catch for nothing to resume took every ValueError, and the data, validation and map errors are ValueErrors.
findings.fix: One error of its own (NothingToResume) is raised by the walk, the solution team and the service when no pause is open, and only it is caught.

findings.defect: The wizard's build route built directly with the switch on, and nothing said so.
findings.scenario: A tester's command line or the wizard built a draft past the walk and its critic while the owner believed the switch covered every build.
findings.cause: The switch was wired to Home's one-step build only, and the exception was written in the record, not in the code.
findings.fix: The exception is stated in the switch's settings and on the route: the wizard is where the person sets the solution field by field, and its build stays direct.

findings.defect: The wiring of a node's budget and of a nested run's spend had no test.
findings.scenario: Removing the walk's parent binding or its node cap left every test green.
findings.cause: The test bound the parent itself and called the cap directly.
findings.fix: A walk with a stub coordinator whose node records a model request in a nested run: the node's cost is that request and the client's limit was set before it acted.

measurements.name: the product flow through the team (upload-team)
measurements.gate: the chat's build goes through the walk, the walk completes, the agent runs the stages, the validator refuses no move
measurements.result: "build it" through the team: 4 hand-offs, the walk completed, the stages run by the agent; holdout roc_auc 0.8416 (95% 0.8211 to 0.8647), logistic regression
measurements.against_gate: Met on Telco with the rules (no model).
limits: One table and no model: the walk asked nothing first on Telco.

measurements.name: the browser check of the Team panel (Chromium)
measurements.gate: a question answered, a confirmation given and the build approved on the page, the draft a project
measurements.result: 5 questions, 1 confirmation and the build approved on the Team panel; the draft built
measurements.against_gate: Met on the delivery-fraud replica's files with the rules.
limits: Headless Chromium on one machine; the rules only.

outcome: A person can walk a draft with the team on Home, answer its pauses there, and with the owner's switch on, Build goes through the team's walk; every walk is bounded by its euro and step budgets, its cost is shown live, and the owner sees every walk on Admin.
lessons: A view of a paused process must show the pause even before the process has produced anything else.
A route that resumes a gate must demand the gate's own permission: the permission of the route is not the permission of the decision it carries.
Read a paused process's state from the process, never from a log that a skipped step does not close.
A pause read from a checkpoint can be stale: before refusing on it, compare it with the state it asks about.
risks: The wizard's step-by-step Build builds directly whatever the switch, by design (said in the settings and on the route).
A pause settled elsewhere is closed by the person's own message in the chat, not on the board, so its board entry stays open.
